doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Buddy Rich: learning a chart in one hearing
summary: Young recalls Buddy Rich on the Tonight Show, who never read music and played an arrangement after hearing the band play it once, and who was hard on some of his men but not on Young.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Buddy Rich came on the Show a lot, I remember seeing Buddy Rich, Buddy Rich on the Tonight Show a lot.

He came on the Tonight Show and he was, he was a good, fun guy too, Buddy Rich was. He would come on the Tonight Show and we would play and I worked with Buddy Rich quite a bit off the band stand, I did. And Buddy Rich, he liked my trumpet playing. He liked my first trumpet playing, that‘s what he liked about me. And you know Buddy Rich didn‘t read no music, you know. Buddy never read a note in his life, but he didn‘t have to read. He was the best drummer that‘d been through here, you know, in a sense you know what I‘m saying. You‘re a drummer, you know what I‘m saying.
No, we all respect Buddy. What was it like, since he didn‘t read, how did he rehearse, how did you play?

You know, funny thing, he would come and tell the band to play the tune down without him. Then he would come up and play right afterwards and that would be what he did. That‘s the way he did it. He‘d tell the band, ―Play the arrangement.‖ He would come up, didn‘t have no music, didn‘t put no music up there, and he would play it, man.
Just one time?
One time. He would do it.
And there‘d be no drummer, or there‘d be another drummer?
Huh?
Would there be a drummer playing or no drums?
I‘m trying to think now if there‘d e a drummer playing.
But, anyways it only took one time.
Only took one time.
You just ran it down, top to bottom, he listened to it, and then come up and play it?
He had the band to play the whole arrangement, one time, and he‘d come up and play it man, and it‘d be just like… he was something else man.
People said he was hard on his own band.

Well, he was tough on some men, man, for some reason, he was. That‘s why I say, he and I got a long, I never had no problem with him. He liked me I guess, because he never did say anything to me, never did. I can‘t say a cross word he gave me, but Buddy Rich did give some guys some cane, man. And I know it, I heard about it, but I wasn‘t one of them, you see? So, I don‘t know what to say about that, you know. I couldn‘t say nothing nice about him if he‘d done something to me.
Right. [laughs]
You see what I‘m saying?
Okay. [laughs]

I couldn‘t say nothing nice about him, as great as he is. If her had done something, he never did cross me up, man, but he did do some things to certain guys, I don‘t know what the reasons were, that‘s not my problem… and I have no idea what it was. And he would get rid of guys too. It must have been something he didn‘t like about them personally, I don‘t know what is was. You‘re a drummer, have you ever heard anything about what might have happened?
Just the same as you, that several of his members had some real difficulties with him, or he gave them a lot of difficulties. He could be hard on his people.

Yeah, right. He was quite a man, man. I was so sorry when we lost him. When he got sick and, went away from here, he didn‘t, there was something about that, he went away from here just… if I‘m right, it wasn‘t like he got sick or anything. He just said, ―Well, see you later, I‘m gone.‖ One of them type of things. That‘s the way he left here,
